+// The cargo-dist shell installer resolves binaries through the archive's
+// top-level directory name; "./"-prefixed members (from `tar -C dir .`)
+// break it with mv ENOENT. rc.7 shipped that breakage from the macOS
+// signing repack — fail closed if it ever reappears.
+function assertInstallableArchiveLayout(name, file) {
+  if (!(name.endsWith(".tar.xz") || name.endsWith(".tar.gz") || name.endsWith(".tgz"))) {
+    return;
+  }
+  const listing = spawnSync("tar", ["-tf", file], { encoding: "utf8" });
+  if (listing.status !== 0) {
+    throw new Error(`tar -tf failed for ${name}: ${listing.stderr}`);
+  }
+  for (const member of listing.stdout.split("\n").filter(Boolean)) {
+    if (member === "." || member === "./" || member.startsWith("./")) {
+      throw new Error(
+        `${name} contains './'-prefixed member ${member}; repack with explicit top-level names or the shell installer breaks`,
+      );
+    }
+  }
+}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-10 00:09:11Z)**_

Based on my analysis, I've examined the full diff and the surrounding code. Let me trace the critical flows:

**Phase 1 — Sinks touched:**
- `releaseFiles` (filesystem walk, dedup by basename) → feeds writeChecksums, writeManifest, verifyManifest
- `assertInstallableArchiveLayout` (new `spawnSync("tar", "-tf", file)`)
- `repackArchive` in sign-macos-artifacts.mjs — **changed from `tar ... .` to `tar ... ...entries`**

**Phase 2 — Tracing the tar argument change in `repackArchive`:**

The diff replaces `tar -cJf archive -C sourceDir .` with `tar -cJf archive -C sourceDir ...entries`, where `entries = fs.readdirSync(sourceDir)` and `sourceDir` was just populated by extracting an attacker/upstream-controlled archive. Previously, `.` was the only positional arg — safe. Now, filenames from the extracted archive flow as positional args to tar.

macOS `tar` is `bsdtar` (libarchive), which supports `--use-compress-program=PROG`, `--newer-mtime`, and similar options. If an archive being signed contains a top-level entry like `--use-compress-program=touch /tmp/pwned`, the extraction creates that file, then `readdirSync` returns it, then `tar` interprets it as an option flag → arbitrary command execution on the signing runner (which holds `APPLE_CERT_P12`, `APPLE_APP_PWD`, etc.).

The `assertInstallableArchiveLayout` verifier in release-trust.mjs does NOT catch this — it only rejects `./`-prefixed members; a `--use-compress-program=...` member sails through.

The diff's own comment says "Pack the top-level entries by name" — the safe fix is to also pass `--` to terminate option parsing before the entries.

**Other paths checked & cleared:**
- `releaseFiles` basename dedup fails closed on content conflict (good)
- `verifyManifest` basename→relative lookup preserves sha256 integrity check (good)
- Nested SHA256SUMS / release-manifest.json exclusion broadened (hardening, not weakening)
- `assertInstallableArchiveLayout` spawnSync uses no shell (good)
- Test-file changes are read-only fixtures

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-10 00:09:34Z)**_

I found one finding: a tar argument-injection regression in `repackArchive`.

The diff changed the macOS repack from `tar ... -C sourceDir .` (safe — `.` is the sole positional) to `tar ... -C sourceDir ...entries`, where `entries` are filenames read directly from the just-extracted archive. macOS bsdtar (libarchive) recognizes option-shaped positionals such as `--use-compress-program=<cmd>`, which spawns `<cmd>`. A top-level archive member named `--use-compress-program=touch /tmp/pwned` would survive extraction, surface from `readdirSync`, and be passed to `tar` as an option — executing arbitrary commands on the signing runner that holds `APPLE_CERT_P12` / `APPLE_APP_PWD`. The new `assertInstallableArchiveLayout` verifier in `release-trust.mjs` only rejects `./`-prefixed members and does not catch this. Recommended fix: insert a `--` end-of-options separator before the entries (or prefix each entry with `./` and relax the verifier accordingly).
